title: Arrays and problem solving — Java Practice
description: Independent practice: A weather station summarizes daily temperatures. Seven questions with explanations.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a safe starting maximum for a known nonempty int array?
questions.explanation: An actual element handles arrays containing only negative values.

questions.prompt: How does a one-pass linear scan grow with n elements?
questions.explanation: It examines at most a constant amount of work per element.

questions.prompt: Does cloning an int[][] deep-copy all rows?

options.text: Only if all rows are equal length

questions.explanation: The outer clone still refers to the original row arrays.

questions.prompt: What value fills a newly allocated int[3]?
Which case exposes initializing maximum to zero incorrectly?

options.text: An array with one positive value
An array of only negative numbers
An array with a positive maximum
An array with a zero maximum

questions.explanation: Zero would incorrectly exceed every real reading.

questions.prompt: What must you decide for a maximum operation on an empty array?
questions.explanation: There is no maximum element; reject or represent absence deliberately.
max = -3, the first actual reading. 4 > -3, so max becomes 4. 1 is not greater than 4; max stays 4.
